# Plan: remove unverifiable and untrusted dependencies from the fork

## Why

This fork is byte-identical to yquake2 master at 9dbf6992 (2026-10-15). The
owner intends to run and extend it without trusting code they cannot read or
verify. A three-way comparison against id Software's 2001 GPL release showed
the fork is roughly 47% id-derived, 35% written by yquake2 contributors since
2009, and 18% vendored third-party code. The fork fixes every high-severity
remote defect present in the 2001 code, so the fork stays the base. What
remains is to shrink the trust surface to: id-derived engine code, the SDL
glue, and the OS.

Principles, in priority order:

1. Nothing that cannot be read in full stays in the tree. A vendored file is
   acceptable only if it is small enough to audit line by line and its hash
   is recorded.
2. Nothing is fetched at build time. The Makefile is the only build. External
   libraries are limited to SDL3 and the OS, and SDL3's provenance is a
   recorded decision (INFORM), not an accident of `brew install`.
3. Defaults favour the untrusted-network case. The engine will be used
   offline or against servers the owner controls, so features that exist only
   to talk to arbitrary servers (HTTP downloads) are removed, not merely
   disabled.
4. Every removal updates `CLAUDE.md`, `doc/`, and the dependency manifest in
   the same change, so the documentation never claims a capability the build
   no longer has.
5. The gate (`scripts/test.sh`, builds q2ded + game) stays green on every
   commit. Changes to client-only code must at minimum compile their
   translation units (`cc -fsyntax-only` with the Makefile's include flags)
   until SDL3 is available on the build machine. No Homebrew packages or
   other dependencies are installed without the owner's explicit approval.

## Security residuals to fix first

These are inherited from the 2001 code and still live in the fork. They are
independent of any removal and go first.

- `svc_download` handler writes `size` bytes from the message without checking
  against the remaining message length (client download parser).
- Savegame directory validation prints "Bad savedir" and continues (server save
  and load commands).
- Collision BSP loader does not validate lump offset+length against file length
  nor plane/child indices in nodes. MD2 loader checks `ofs_end` but not inner
  offsets. Cinematic Huffman decoder trusts counts and node indices from the
  file. Frame areabits length byte is not bounded to the array.

## Audits after removal

- Network message parsers (client-side `cl_parse.c`, server-side `sv_user.c`,
  `sv_conless.c`, `movemsg.c`, `netchan.c`): every read bounded, every index
  checked. Findings become cards.
- Asset loaders (`collision.c`, `refresh/files/*`, `cl_cin.c`, `wave.c`, pak
  directory parsing in `filesystem.c`).
- Small vendored files kept (gyro.c, md4.c, rand.c, glob.c, savegame tables):
  full read, hash recorded in the dependency manifest.

## Dependency manifest and verification

`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` lists every remaining external library and every
in-tree third-party file with version, provenance URL, license and sha256.
`scripts/check-vendored.sh` verifies the hashes and becomes part of the gate.
Any future vendored addition must update both.

## Fork documentation

Common practice for a long-lived fork, which this plan adopts:

- Keep `LICENSE` and every copyright notice unchanged (the GPL requires it).
- Rewrite `README.md` to say what this repository is: a fork of Yamagi Quake
  II, which upstream commit it was taken from and when, why it exists, and
  how it differs. One "Upstream" section credits yquake2, id Software and
  Icculus with links. Bug reports, releases and CI references point at this
  repository, not upstream.
- Add `FORK.md` (or a section in README) recording provenance and the sync
  policy: the `upstream` remote, which upstream changes are cherry-picked
  (security fixes), which are not (new dependencies, features).
- Keep upstream's `CHANGELOG` as history and start a fork changelog above it
  or in a separate file.
- Keep `doc/` and annotate where this fork's behaviour differs (removed
  features, changed defaults). Remove or redirect links that point at
  upstream's issue tracker, release page and CI.
- Do not rename the project until it diverges enough that calling it Yamagi
  Quake II would mislead users. Record that decision (INFORM).

## Order of work

1. Security residuals (independent, small).
2. High-confidence removals: curl, OpenAL, GLES renderers, CMake/winbuild/zip,
   CI pinning, minizip/miniz, stb_image_write, SDL2 paths.
3. INFORM-gated removals once the owner closes the decision cards: stb_vorbis,
   stb_image, GL3, SDL3 vendoring, CI platform scope.
4. Audits on what remains; manifest and hash check into the gate.
5. Fork documentation throughout, finalised after the removals settle.

## Repository access

Policy: the fork stays public and read-only for everyone except the owner.
Nobody else can push, open issues or pull requests, or comment; `main`
cannot be force-pushed or deleted, enforced server-side. There are no
collaborators by decision, so "collaborators only" means "owner only".
Recorded by TASK26 on 2026-10-18 from the owner's own `gh` login, completed
2026-10-19.

| Control | State | How it was checked |
|---|---|---|
| Issue creation | `COLLABORATORS_ONLY` (verified 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19) | GraphQL `repository.issueCreationPolicy` |
| Pull request creation | `COLLABORATORS_ONLY` (verified 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19) | GraphQL `repository.pullRequestCreationPolicy` |
| Issues / Pull requests enabled | both `true` (the loop files cards and lands work through them) | same read |
| Interaction limit | `collaborators_only`, expires 2027-04-18T17:57:18Z | `GET repos/BeauBender/quake2/interaction-limits` |
| Ruleset `main-protect` on `main` | active since 2026-10-19 (applied by the owner, ruleset id 25424093): rules `deletion` + `non_fast_forward`, target `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`, no bypass actors on purpose (the agent runs as the owner, so an owner bypass would exempt it too) | `GET repos/BeauBender/quake2/rules/branches/main` lists exactly those two rules; the live ruleset's name, target, enforcement, conditions, rules and bypass list are identical to `.github/rulesets/main-protect.json` |
| Conversation locks | every issue and PR locked: #1–#34 on 2026-10-18, #35–#76 on 2026-10-19 | `GET repos/BeauBender/quake2/issues?state=all` returns no unlocked conversation; locks never expire, but new conversations arrive unlocked, so each new card or PR is locked right after it is created (`gh api -X PUT repos/BeauBender/quake2/issues/<n>/lock`) |
| GitHub Apps with access | reviewed by the owner on 2026-10-19; the list is kept out of this public record, because it names the third-party credentials that can reach the repo. Removing an app is the owner's decision | not listable with a user OAuth token (`GET user/installations` returns 403); the owner read Settings → Integrations → GitHub Apps |
| Code review limits ("Limit to users explicitly granted read or higher access") | applied by the owner on 2026-10-19 | UI only: Settings → Moderation → Code review limits |

Deferred on purpose:

- `main-require-pr.json` (require a pull request before merging): the memory
  sync Stop hook and the breakdown plan-anchor commit still push straight
  to `main`; enabling it would break the loop until those paths change.
- Required status checks: Actions now runs on every pull request, and the
  loop already refuses to merge on a red or pending check
  (`merge.ciChecks: require` in `.claude/dev-loop.json`). Making checks
  required server-side is not decided yet; GitHub sometimes cancels the
  macOS job for lack of a runner, and a required check that never reports
  blocks the merge.
- Going private: not possible for a fork ("You cannot change the visibility
  of a fork by itself").

Renewal: the interaction limit is six months at most by GitHub design; the
same `PUT` re-applies it. No automation keeps locks and the limit current yet: lock-on-create and
interaction-limit renewal automation does not exist, so renewal is a manual
owner step recorded here.
